requirements.requirement: Repair bin/prune so it removes only .thumb cache entries absent from active.txt and strictly older than the supplied cutoff, while treating symbolic links as links rather than following them.
requirements.summary: The installed Perl 5.8-compatible implementation validates the epoch, reads active.txt, examines only cache entries ending in .thumb, uses lstat, applies a strict mtime < cutoff comparison, and unlinks eligible regular files or links. Isolated behavior tests retained an active old file, a cutoff-equal file, a newer inactive file, and a non-cache README; they removed an old inactive file and later an eligible symlink without changing its target.

requirements.requirement: Remove the obsolete live thumbnail entries while leaving active entries, newer inactive entries, non-cache files, source media, and protected symlinks unchanged.
requirements.summary: The live run removed all 256 obsolete thumbnails and left zero remaining. Pre/post checksums match for active.txt, policy.txt, keep-active.thumb, keep-new.thumb, README, and source media. The newer media-link.thumb remained the same symlink and target, and a second run removed zero entries. The same clean and protected state was observed after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic were unchanged before and after execution/restart. The repaired script passed syntax checks under the installed Perl 5.8.8 and continued working after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral and final-state evidence. The node-restart protocol is complete: it captured a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, restart acknowledgement, observed bounded unavailability, a different post-restart boot ID, and recovered script/data state. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: Failed-service inspection was unsupported on this legacy non-systemd platform, so lifecycle evidence cannot independently rule out failed services; no task-related service was involved.
Lifecycle snapshots do not inventory the task fixture itself; fixture correctness instead relies on the detailed executor pre/post checks and post-restart verification.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1
